title: Hadamard sensing channel: deterministic artifact suppression for quantum sensors
abstract: Dynamical decoupling sequences are essential for nanoscale quantum sensing, but the finite duration of microwave pulses generates spurious responses. While phase randomization (PR) protocol can suppress these artifacts, they rely on probabilistic averaging. This introduces an inherent statistical variance that demands excessive sequence lengths and stringent hardware capabilities for true random phase generation. Here, we propose Hadamard sensing channel (HSC), a deterministic phase-design framework based on Hadamard matrices. HSC completely eliminates the statistical variance of PR by exactly and deterministically canceling spurious signals using a finite set of orthogonal phase patterns. Simulations confirm that HSC matches the ideal suppression of PR but exhibits superior robustness against control errors. HSC offers a mathematically exact and hardware-friendly solution for reliable high-resolution nanoscale nuclear magnetic resonance.
summary: This paper introduces the Hadamard Sensing Channel (HSC), a deterministic technique to suppress spurious signals that degrade quantum sensor readings due to imperfect microwave pulses. By leveraging the orthogonality of Hadamard matrices, HSC achieves signal cancellation superior to probabilistic methods like Phase Randomization. It offers a robust and hardware-efficient solution for high-fidelity nanoscale magnetometry.
main_problem: Spurious responses generated by finite duration microwave pulses during dynamical decoupling sequences compromise quantum sensing fidelity in nanoscale systems.
main_result: The proposed Hadamard Sensing Channel (HSC) deterministically cancels these spurious signals using a finite set of orthogonal phase patterns, matching ideal suppression while being more robust than probabilistic methods.
method: HSC employs a deterministic phase-design framework based on Hadamard matrices to average out unwanted signal components over a finite number of runs.
model_or_system: The study models quantum sensors, specifically using Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond for nanoscale nuclear magnetic resonance. The system evolution is governed by a Hamiltonian involving spin operators and time-dependent fields.
key_observables: Transition probability related to the sensor's remaining coherence ($\langle \hat{S}_x angle$) and the Fourier amplitude of spurious responses ($f_{\perp}$).
important_parameters: The number of runs, $M$, which dictates the suppression factor; control error parameters like pulse angle errors and detuning.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that exploiting the orthogonality of Hadamard matrices provides a sufficient basis for deterministic cancellation, even if it deviates from strict abelian group constructions.

paper_structure: The paper first identifies spurious responses in DD sequences. It then contrasts existing methods (PR) with its novel HSC approach, deriving the suppression mechanism using Hadamard matrix properties, and finally validating performance through simulations comparing HSC against PR under realistic control errors.
why_interesting: This work provides a mathematically exact and hardware-friendly protocol for mitigating systematic errors in quantum sensing measurements, which is crucial for advancing high-resolution magnetometry experiments involving open quantum systems.
